newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Newswomen's Club announces awards.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Newswomen's Club announces awards.

text.p: Reuters won two awards Monday from the prestigious Newswomen's Club of New York, one for a feature on the mysterious disappearance of a judge and the other for a column on collecting Barbies as an investment.

Ellen Wulfhorst, Reuters' New York correspondent, won the award in the general wire service category for her story on Joseph Crater, a New York State judge who caught a cab in midtown Manhattan in 1930 and completely vanished.

Maureen Bavdek, a rewrite editor for Reuters' Americas desk, won in the financial wire service category for her column on Barbie collectibles, ranging from the first Barbie in 1959 to the Gold Jubilee doll made for Barbie's 35th anniversary.
The Newswomen's Club was founded in 1922 when women were barred from joining male-only press clubs.
The winners will be honoured at the club's Front Page Awards dinner in New York on Nov 14.

Other winners included reporters Michelle Caruso and Molly Gordy at New York's Daily News; Jennifer Gonnerman of the Village Voice; Celia Dugger and Michiko Kakutani of The New York Times; Beth Whitehouse of Newsday and Ellen Schultz of the Wall Street Journal; Stevie Lacy-Pendleton of the Staten Island Advance.
Winners of the photography awards were Susan Watts of the Daily News, Kathy Knonicek of Newsday and Annie Liebovitz for a photo essay in Vanity Fair.
Awards in the magazine category went to Joan Acocella of The New Yorker, Marie Brenner at Vanity Fair and Mary Kuntz, Business Week.

Television awards went to Cynthia McFadden and Lisa Cohen of ABC News Primetime Live; Denise Schreiner and Meredith Viera of ABC News Turning Point; and Mary Murphy of WPIX. Radio awards went to Alice Stockton Rossini of 1010 WINS and Laura Sydell of WNYC.
